correctness.rationale: The proof uses the quotient universal property. A graded map is one degree-one matrix; every column must have vanishing dth power. If d=p^s Frobenius imposes no constraints. Otherwise with d=p^s*u, p∤u and u>1, the surviving mixed coefficient binom(d,p^s)=u modulo p forces at most one nonzero coefficient per column. Full rank and idempotent formulas follow from Gaussian surjections, inclusion-exclusion on occupied coordinate rows, and complements to image planes, with image algebra dimension d^r from graded automorphisms or coordinate spans. Exact independent quotient-relation and idempotence enumeration passed 18 finite cases including F4. Neither finite checks nor numerical evidence are offered as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Monomial complete intersections are a standard foundational class of Artinian algebras. Graded retraction-image geometry changes categorically at a pure characteristic-power exponent: all linear subspaces versus only coordinate supports. The classification of the full graded map monoid and all rank/individual image fibers in both phases gives a natural complete structural invariant for every n,d,q, rather than a small numerical slice or a routine known-table recomputation.
